findings.title: Inefficient glob traversal on ignored directories
findings.description: repo.glob(pattern) recursively traverses all directories including large ignored ones like node_modules and .venv before filtering them. This causes significant blocking disk I/O and memory bloat on large codebases.
findings.suggestion: Implement a custom traversal (e.g., using os.walk) that explicitly skips excluded directories before entering them, rather than generating all paths and filtering post-traversal.

findings.title: Sensitive .env files transmitted to third-party APIs
findings.description: The security focus explicitly gathers '**/*.env*' files. Since Noxaudit sends gathered file contents to external LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) for analysis, this results in actual production or development secrets being transmitted over the network to third parties.
findings.suggestion: Remove .env files from the gathered file patterns. If secret scanning is needed for .env files, use a local rule-based regex scanner rather than an external LLM.

findings.title: No test coverage for GitHub issues data mutation
findings.description: The issues.py module creates issues on GitHub via the gh CLI but has zero test coverage. This is a critical data mutation path where bugs could cause duplicate issue spam or fail to report critical security vulnerabilities.
findings.suggestion: Add a tests/test_issues.py file with mocked subprocess.run calls to verify issue creation, deduplication logic, and rate-limiting behavior.

findings.title: Duplicated LLM JSON parsing logic
findings.description: The code to extract JSON blocks from Markdown and map them to Finding objects is duplicated between _parse_text and _parse_response. The same exact boilerplate is also repeated in openai.py and anthropic.py.
findings.suggestion: Extract the JSON parsing and Finding object mapping logic into a shared helper function in BaseProvider or a common utils module.

findings.title: Action installs from unpinned git branch
findings.description: The GitHub Action installs noxaudit via 'pip install git+https://github.com/atriumn/noxaudit.git', which pulls the default branch on every run. This exposes users to supply chain risks and sudden breaking changes.
findings.suggestion: Install the package directly from PyPI with a pinned version constraint, or pin the git installation to a specific commit SHA or release tag matching the action's version.

findings.title: Inconsistent dev dependency pinning
findings.description: The project uses both [project.optional-dependencies] dev (PEP 621) and [dependency-groups] dev (PEP 735) with conflicting version constraints for pytest (>=8.0 vs >=9.0.2) and ruff (>=0.8 vs >=0.15.1).
findings.suggestion: Consolidate the development dependencies into a single section or ensure both sections enforce the exact same version constraints.

findings.title: Unbounded memory usage when hashing files
findings.description: The _hash_file function reads the entire file contents into memory using path.read_bytes() before computing the SHA256 hash. If called on very large files, this could cause severe memory spikes.
findings.suggestion: Read the file in fixed-size chunks (e.g., 8192 bytes) and update the hash incrementally to maintain a constant memory footprint.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for Telegram network calls
findings.description: The telegram notification module makes network requests via httpx but has no corresponding unit tests. Error handling, HTTP timeouts, and correct payload formatting are entirely untested.
findings.suggestion: Add tests using a library like respx or httpx_mock to verify the Telegram integration works correctly under both success and failure conditions.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling for invalid CLI inputs
findings.description: The 'estimate' command catches ValueError and raises a clean click.ClickException, but the 'run' and 'submit' commands do not catch ValueError from _resolve_focus_names or run_audit, leading to raw Python stack traces being dumped to the user.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same try/except block used in 'estimate' to 'run' and 'submit' to consistently convert expected ValueErrors into clean ClickExceptions.

findings.title: Path Traversal vulnerability in report saving
findings.description: The reports_path is constructed via 'Path(reports_dir) / repo'. Because 'repo' comes directly from the user-controlled noxaudit.yml config, a malicious repository name like '../../' could write report files outside the designated reports directory.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize the 'repo' variable (e.g., by ensuring it doesn't contain path separators) before using it to construct the file path.

findings.title: Stale/dead configuration field for webhooks
findings.description: The NotificationConfig dataclass and config parser include a 'webhook' field which is also documented in the CLI reference, but the application logic in runner.py only supports the 'telegram' channel, making 'webhook' dead configuration.
findings.suggestion: Remove the 'webhook' field from the dataclass and documentation, or fully implement the webhook notification logic in runner.py.

findings.title: Heavy dependency used for simple POST request
findings.description: The project depends on 'httpx>=0.27', but it is only used for a single, optional POST request in the Telegram notification module. This brings in a large dependency tree unnecessarily.
findings.suggestion: Replace the httpx.post call with Python's built-in urllib.request to remove the httpx dependency and reduce the package footprint.

findings.title: Synchronous blocking operations in async context
findings.description: The MCP server uses 'async def' endpoints, but performs blocking synchronous operations within them (e.g., subprocess.run and path.read_text()). This blocks the async event loop and degrades server concurrency.
findings.suggestion: Replace blocking subprocess calls with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec and wrap blocking file I/O in asyncio.to_thread().

findings.title: Sequential blocking LLM audits
findings.description: When multiple repositories are configured, the run_audit function processes them in a sequential loop (_run_repo_sync). This blocks synchronously on the LLM API calls, which can take minutes per repo, artificially increasing total execution time.
findings.suggestion: Parallelize the repository audit loops using concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor or asyncio to execute API calls concurrently.

findings.title: Path Traversal in LLM-controlled file paths
findings.description: In create_baseline_decisions, finding.file is passed to _hash_file without sanitization. Because finding.file originates from the LLM's JSON output, a prompt injection attack could force the LLM to return a path like '../../../../etc/shadow', which Noxaudit would then open and read into memory.
findings.suggestion: Validate that finding.file resolves strictly within the intended repo_path before attempting to read and hash the file.
